macro.story:
Start with the facts. SPY closed at $741 (+1.65% on the day, -0.46% over five days), QQQ +2.49% on the day with the Nasdaq up 2.07% — both indices sit above their 50- and 200-day moving averages but the daily MACD remains below signal (SPY histogram -1.90, QQQ -3.11), so the bounce is happening inside a still-tired momentum picture. RSI is mid-range across the board (SPY 52, QQQ 53, Nasdaq 49), the VIX is 17.58 and has actually fallen ~10% over five days, and the Dollar Index sits at 101.4 with RSI 68.5 in a clean uptrend (+2.5% over 21 days). Commodities are the broken leg: Gold -2.2% / 5d, -11.4% / 21d; Silver -4.4% / 5d, -21.6% / 21d; WTI crude -2.6% / 5d, -18.4% / 21d, with oil RSI at 31.6 — washed out, not yet turning.

The tracked conversation today leans net bearish, roughly 3-to-1 against bulls with the bulk of voices neutral. The prevailing sentiment attributes the bid in mega-cap tech to a one-day risk-on pop following geopolitical de-escalation news (Iran-related), with the dominant view flagging two longer-running concerns: skyrocketing AI-related investment-grade debt issuance (projected +25% with 2026 gross supply at a record ~$2.25T) and contracting employment in AI-affected sectors (-11k monthly jobs on the 3-month average). Sentiment also notes the Yen collapsing to its weakest versus the Dollar since 1986 — which is consistent with the DXY data on the screen. This is the key alignment/conflict read: sentiment is leaning bearish on tech fundamentals at the same moment the structured rotation data is showing leadership rotating AWAY from tech (Technology and Communication Services are weak/bearish) and INTO Industrials, Financials, Healthcare, and Utilities. The narrative and the tape agree that the leadership mantle is changing hands — they disagree only on whether what's underneath qualifies as a healthy rotation or a slow-motion top.

Under the index surface, seven of eleven GICS sectors are above their 50-day, with Industrials, Financials, Healthcare, Utilities, and Consumer Staples all HOT and breadth balanced (S&P 500 bullish 54.8% vs bearish 28.7%). The rotation radar lights up four validated Early-Runway industries: Travel Services, Diagnostics & Research, Credit Services, and Drug Manufacturers – Specialty & Generic. Energy and Materials are the explicit losers, consistent with the commodity collapse and the dominant sentiment view that oil's risk premium is being wrung out. Dollar strength is a validated headwind for gold and silver — that inverse relationship is firing cleanly here.

Forward watch: the macro is genuinely transitional — not washed out (no Engine C bounce signal, SPY only -2.8% from 52w high, washout state CALM), not euphoric (VIX 17.6, breadth balanced, no major index RSI > 70). Confidence is MEDIUM because trend and breadth are constructive but daily MACD is negative on the headline indices and the dominant sentiment lean is bearish — the disagreement is real. Hunt longs inside the Early-Runway industries where the validated rotation signal is active; avoid forcing exposure in tech, energy, materials, or metals until those internals turn.

DXY at 101.37 is up 2.4% over 21 days, sitting above both its 21d and 50d SMAs with RSI at 67.9 — the ACTIVE DXY_METALS_TAG signal is firing, and the metals complex is paying the bill. Gold -11.5% on 21d, Silver -21.3%, and the Precious Metals theme has been formally tagged FADING. Every other narrative this week — sector rotation, commodity unwind, even the bid in TLT — is downstream of this one move.

**[CROSS-ASSET LENS]** The regime reads CHOPPY/TRANSITIONAL at 8/10 confidence with breadth a tepid 63.6% above 50SMA, but the macro plumbing is not panicked: VIX 17.67 in contango with VIX3M at 20.13, SPY RSI a neutral 52.3, put/call constructive. Oil at $71.32 with RSI 31.9 is oversold but the WTI mean-reversion signal is WEAK — it's a downtrend, not a setup.

**[SECTOR & ROTATION LENS]** Money is flowing into defensives and domestically-oriented cyclicals while tech digests. XLV +7.0%, XLI +5.4%, XLF +5.2%, XLU +3.8% on 21d — that's a classic stronger-dollar, lower-long-end rotation profile. XLK -0.7% and QQQ -1.5% on 21d despite XLK still tagged ACCELERATING_BULLISH on trajectory — the trend is intact but the relative bid has cooled. IWM +2.6% confirms the domestic tilt: small caps benefit when DXY is firm and the 10Y is range-bound. XLB -1.0% rounds out the commodity unwind.

**[WHERE THE OPPORTUNITY IS]** The Semiconductors run is in ceiling territory — HOT 13 months, +258% gain (a record on our books), CEILING flag triggered. That's exits-not-entries, even though trajectory still reads HOLDING_BULLISH. The interesting setups are early-innings: Software - Infrastructure is HOT just 1 month with only +3% accrued versus a +18% typical run — early in the spell with ACCELERATING_BULLISH trajectory. Internet Content & Information sits in the same posture — 1 month in, still net -5%, plenty of runway if the trend holds. For coiled-not-yet-run names with bullish flow: MA and SOFI in Credit Services (coils 85.7% and 70.9%), and LMND in P&C Insurance (74.6%) — these haven't extended on 5d or 21d, so entries aren't chasing.

**[WHAT TO WATCH]** The tripwire is DXY 101.37 holding above the 50d. If DXY rolls back below its 21d SMA, the metals fade unwinds fast and the defensive rotation loses its tailwind — XLV/XLF leadership would likely cede back to XLK and QQQ. Conversely, a 2Y yield close above its current upper-band print would reinforce dollar strength and keep the pressure on Gold, Silver, and Copper. Also flag: precious metals just had a washout-style move; 88% of washout lows get retested within 60 days, so any bounce in GLD/SLV here is suspect until proven otherwise.
